section_summary: This section contains the June 3, 1946 despatch from the American Embassy in Brussels reporting on archives recovered from the former Japanese Embassy, together with duplicate copies and supporting enclosures. The enclosures catalogue motion-picture films, identify former embassy employees and their relatives, and reproduce detailed Japanese classifications of Belgian journalists, officials, academics, businessmen, and activists as neutral, pro-Japanese, or anti-Japanese. The files illuminate Japanese cultural propaganda, press relations, political networking, and personnel administration in prewar Belgium.

subfiles.title: List of Motion Picture Films (continuation)
subfiles.about: Continuation of an inventory of Japanese cultural, propaganda, travel, industrial, and wartime motion-picture films.
subfiles.summary: The pages continue at item 11 and list films concerning wartime destruction, Japanese scenery, sports, schools, fishing, arts, tea, silk, agriculture, and seasonal festivals. Titles appear in English, French, and Dutch, with film gauges and reel counts. Several entries concern China, including the fall of Hankow and the Sino-Japanese conflict.

subfiles.title: List of Persons Believed to Be Japanese Embassy Employees
subfiles.about: Identifies employees and household associates of the former Japanese Embassy in Brussels.
subfiles.summary: The list records names, birthplaces and dates, addresses, occupations, nationalities, and family relationships. It includes translators, porters, drivers, servants, stenographers, and waiters, together with their relatives. Several later entries cite identity cards, employment dates, wages, and Japanese annotations in the source volumes.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 219: Japanese Archives in Brussels
subfiles.about: Transmits additional information recovered from the archives of the former Japanese Embassy in Brussels.
subfiles.summary: The despatch responds to Department airgram A-130 of April 25, 1946. It forwards three enclosures: an index of pro- and anti-Japanese persons, a motion-picture film inventory, and a list of former Japanese Embassy employees. The despatch is marked restricted.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1: Index of Pro-Japanese, Anti-Japanese, and Neutral Persons
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels, transcribing former Japanese Embassy records
subfiles.about: Reproduces the Japanese Embassy's political and attitudinal classification of influential Belgian contacts.
subfiles.summary: An alphabetical index labels Belgian journalists, officials, academics, military officers, clergy, and businessmen as neutral, Japanophile, or Japanophobe. Detailed dossiers give professions, addresses, publications, travel, organizational ties, and contacts with Japanese officials. The records emphasize cultural lectures, press influence, economic missions, Manchukuo advocacy, and public support for China during the Sino-Japanese conflict.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2: List of Motion Picture Films
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels, from former Japanese Embassy holdings
subfiles.about: Catalogues 85 reels or groups of reels found in the former Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The inventory includes films on Hirohito's European journey, the League of Nations inquiry in Manchuria, Japanese investment and industry, the 1923 earthquake, and the Sino-Japanese conflict. It also lists extensive cultural and travel films on Japanese cities, arts, gardens, pottery, tea, silk, agriculture, fishing, seasons, and festivals. Film gauges, reel counts, labels, and possible censorship fragments are noted.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3: List of Persons Believed to Be Japanese Embassy Employees
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels, transcribing former Japanese Embassy records
subfiles.about: Provides multilingual personnel and household records for people associated with the former Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: German- and French-language entries identify translators, porters, secretaries, chauffeurs, servants, and waiters, as well as spouses and other relatives. The records supply birth information, addresses, nationality, identity-card references, dates of service, wages, and dismissal information. Notes indicate that several original entries carried Japanese writing.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 219: Japanese Archives in Brussels (duplicate copy)
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the despatch transmitting information from the former Japanese Embassy archives.
subfiles.summary: This copy again cites airgram A-130 and describes the same three enclosures. It summarizes the index of political attitudes, film inventory, and employee list forwarded to the Department. The document is marked restricted.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1: Index of Pro-Japanese, Anti-Japanese, and Neutral Persons (duplicate copy)
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels, transcribing former Japanese Embassy records
subfiles.about: Duplicate transcription of the Japanese Embassy's classifications and dossiers on Belgian contacts.
subfiles.summary: The enclosure repeats the alphabetical summary and detailed neutral, Japanophile, and Japanophobe files. It records professional positions, addresses, writings, Japanese contacts, East Asian travel, and attitudes toward the Sino-Japanese conflict. This copy clarifies several names and passages obscured in the earlier copy.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2: List of Motion Picture Films (duplicate copy)
subfiles.from: American Embassy, Brussels, from former Japanese Embassy holdings
subfiles.about: Duplicate inventory of the motion-picture films held by the former Japanese Embassy.
subfiles.summary: The list again describes 85 film entries ranging from diplomatic and Manchurian subjects to Japanese travel, arts, industry, agriculture, and festivals. It includes bilingual title cards, reel sizes, gauges, and notes on unidentified or possibly censored fragments. The closing entries cover silk making, doll making, fishing, rice cultivation, seasons, and Japanese festivals.
